title: Farage Wins Clacton as Watchdog Probe Resumes, Trump Orders Navy Back to Steam Catapults, US Calls West Bank Settlers 'Terrorists'
subhead: Reform UK's Nigel Farage returns to Parliament but faces a revived ethics investigation; the White House orders a costly rollback of the Navy's electromagnetic catapults; and Washington issues an unusually sharp rebuke of Israeli settler violence in the West Bank.

sections.heading: Farage Back in Parliament, but the Watchdog Is Waiting
sections.body:
Reform UK leader Nigel Farage won the Clacton on Sea by-election on Friday, returning to the House of Commons after abruptly quitting his seat in July. AP reports he beat a field of 34 candidates, including serial challenger Count Binface, after the major parties boycotted the contest as a political stunt. Farage declared victory in the early morning and did not attend the official declaration.

The win is not the end of the story. A parliamentary watchdog investigation into whether Farage failed to report a 5 million pound ($6.7 million) gift from an overseas crypto billionaire was suspended when he stepped down, but AP reports it was resumed hours after the result was announced. That means Farage could be forced out of Parliament again and face yet another election.
sections.whyItMatters: Farage is seen by some as a possible next prime minister, but the revived ethics probe keeps a legal sword hanging over his return — a reminder that his political trajectory now runs through a compliance process, not just the ballot box.

sections.heading: Trump Orders the Navy Back to Steam Catapults
sections.body:
President Donald Trump issued a directive Thursday ordering the Navy to remove the Electromagnetic Aircraft Launch System (EMALS) from its newest Ford-class carriers and return to older steam catapults, according to AP. The memo directs the Pentagon to present plans within two months and also calls for replacing the carriers' electromagnetic weapons elevators.

The move would likely cost billions of dollars and revert the Navy's most advanced ships to a system that requires more sailors and is harder to maintain. AP notes it comes as the military struggles to fund its equipment wish list and the Navy faces a sailor shortage. The contrast is sharp: China's newest carriers use electromagnetic catapults, and France plans the same for its new carrier.
sections.whyItMatters: A costly, ideologically driven rollback of proven technology at a moment of acute naval strain — and a widening gap with China and France on carrier design — raises questions about US naval readiness precisely when carriers are being surged toward the Middle East.

sections.heading: Washington Calls West Bank Settlers 'Terrorists'
sections.body:
For five nights, Israeli settlers surrounded three Palestinian homes in the occupied West Bank village of Qusra, including one owned by a Palestinian American. On Thursday, US Ambassador Mike Huckabee called the settlers 'terrorists,' AP reports — an unusually sharp rebuke from an administration that has given unprecedented support to Israeli settlements.

Huckabee said the actions of those who carried out the siege were 'disgusting.' Israel's military condemned the siege on Tuesday and said Thursday that troops dismantled two illegal outposts. The standoff is the latest in a wave of settler violence convulsing the territory Israel seized in the 1967 war.
sections.whyItMatters: The public break between Washington and settler groups is notable given Trump's pro-settlement record, and it signals the administration is willing to police the West Bank's most volatile flashpoints even as it backs Israel elsewhere.

sections.heading: Two UAE Tankers Hit by Drones in the Strait of Hormuz
sections.body:
Two UAE tankers were attacked by drones while transiting the Strait of Hormuz, AP reports, the latest incident in the ongoing wartime campaign against vessels and infrastructure in and around the waterway. The attacks come as oil residue lines the shore near fishing boats on Iran's Qeshm Island, though AP notes the source of that spill has not been independently determined.

Separately, AP photographs show flames and smoke rising from the port of Mokha in Yemen after a strike on Friday, with an injured child receiving treatment at a hospital. The strikes underscore how the broader Iran-US conflict continues to radiate into the Gulf and Red Sea shipping lanes.
sections.whyItMatters: Drone attacks on commercial tankers in Hormuz keep the world's most critical oil chokepoint in a state of active hazard, sustaining the risk premium on global energy even as diplomatic efforts to reopen the strait continue.

sections.heading: Kushner Heads to Israel and Egypt to Push Gaza Deal
sections.body:
Jared Kushner will travel to the Middle East next week to try to advance plans to end the Gaza conflict, AP reports, after a Trump administration deal for Hamas to disarm ran into Israeli opposition. Kushner, Board of Peace high representative Nickolay Mladenov, and former British Prime Minister Tony Blair are due in Israel on Sunday before traveling to Cairo.

The trip comes after Hamas accepted a plan to decommission its weapons, but Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu said Israel would not withdraw until Hamas has completely disarmed. The deal, based on an October ceasefire that ended major military operations, has stalled on other fronts.
sections.whyItMatters: The high-level visit is a test of whether the US-brokered disarmament framework can survive the gap between Hamas's acceptance and Israel's insistence on full disarmament before any withdrawal.

bottomLine: Today's developments are less about a single dramatic shift than about the machinery of several ongoing crises. Farage's return to Parliament is shadowed by a revived ethics probe; Trump's catapult order injects cost and risk into a Navy already stretched thin; and Washington's sharp rebuke of West Bank settlers marks a notable departure from its usual posture. Meanwhile, drone attacks on tankers in Hormuz and a strike on Yemen's Mokha port keep the Gulf's shipping lanes in active danger, even as Kushner's trip to Israel and Egypt tests whether the Gaza disarmament deal can be revived. The through-line: several fragile arrangements — political, military, and diplomatic — are being stress-tested at once, and none has yet resolved.
